chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Whenever the water overcomes the smell of the carcass, then perform wudu (ablution) from it and drink. But when the water changes and the taste changes, then do not perform wudu (ablution) from it and do not drink.

key_terms.الطَّعْمُ: the taste, indicating alteration of the water
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the water under discussion for purity and use
key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ: underwent change in a legally relevant way
key_terms.رِيحِ الْجِيفَةِ: the odor of a carcass affecting the water
key_terms.غَلَبَ: remained predominant or overpowering in relation to impurity

ai.seo_question: When can water affected by the smell of a carcass still be used for wudu (ablution) and drinking?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water affected by a carcass. If the water remains dominant over the odor and has not changed in a way indicating contamination, it may be used for wudu (ablution) and drinking; but if the water itself changes in taste, it must not be used for either.
